piece_title: The crossing — pure-pursuit steering against the road, the deck parapet, the teleport exclusion in path_m, and the premise correction that replaced the "57.5 degree skirt" with a 471 m viaduct (round 1)

critic.context: Fresh context. No part of W1-CROSSING, W1-ROAD-JOIN, W1-01-r4 or W1-05 was written by me. I wrote three instruments of my own under tools/world/critic-crossing-* and judged on those: a walker with its own per-frame distance accumulator hung off Engine._afterStep (so the distance is not read off the instrument under test), an offline grade/vacuity/stall-site audit sampled straight off game/src/world/field.js, and a three-mode probe (regain, null, deletefix).
critic.load_declaration: node tools/contention.mjs --gate returned exit 3 (WAIT) at 05:44 and 05:46 (load 4.23-4.85 per core against a 4.0 ceiling). I DID NOT PROCEED. I did offline work until the gate returned exit 0 (GO, 1.92 per core) at 05:49 and started the crossing walk then; the gate was GO at every later check. One browser at a time, never concurrent, chained sequentially. NO TIMING OR PERFORMANCE FIGURE IS PUBLISHED ANYWHERE IN THIS VERDICT: every number here is a distance in metres, a frame count, an in-world minute (frames/3600), an angle, a count or a boolean, and none of them move with load. Wall-clock durations are recorded inside the run artifacts for reproduction only and are not quoted as results.
critic.environment_note: The tree was clean at 2fe47f5 for the whole run except for my own declared files. I edited nothing under game/.
method_deviations: tools/world/critic-crossing-walk.mjs — my own walker. It uses the shipped walkRoute/walkPath verbs (they are what is under test) but installs an INDEPENDENT per-frame accumulator on Engine._afterStep that re-derives walked distance from the capsule's own position deltas, keeps the unbounded 'naive' sum as well, and logs every step over 1 m. --kill-at-m forces a death mid-walk so the teleport-exclusion branch can be watched taking. --steer/--clamp/--no-deck install pre-fix code or delete the structure model, each proven to have taken before the arm reports.

tools/world/critic-crossing-grade.mjs — offline. Re-derives the worst longitudinal road gradient from roads.json by its own arithmetic, measures whether the centreline slope-gate counter CAN be non-zero, sweeps the gate laterally across the carriageway with a structure-free control, audits the published stall coordinate against the declared spans, and recounts G3/G4. --self-test bends a leg and requires the report to go red (24.27 -> 89.17 deg).

tools/world/critic-crossing-probe.mjs — --regain rebuilds C5-REGAIN as 20 independent trials; --null replaces C2-NULL-IS-SILENT's inherited bar with a measured noise floor; --deletefix re-runs the 2x2 with the arm order REVERSED and the world re-seeded before every arm.

headline: I WALKED IT, AND THE NUMBERS ARE RIGHT TO THE DECIMAL. 6,646.7 m, 199,433 frames, 55.398 in-world minutes, mean 1.9991 m/s, 0.063% of 33,238 samples under 1.6 m/s, worst deviation 1.39 m, zero frames off the road, zero teleports, ending at (2765.6, 5028.8) — reproduced independently with a second per-frame counter whose UNBOUNDED sum is also 6,646.7 m and whose largest single-frame step in 199,432 frames is 0.295 m, so the zero is zero because nothing jumped. The teleport exclusion was watched catching a real 3,856.1 m respawn. BUT: walkPath was never fixed and the round says it was; the crossing does not walk backwards (STUCK at 5,072.3 m against a bridge deck laid across its own switchback); and one of the three supports the premise correction rests on is a counter that is 100% exempt by construction.

reference_items.native_scale: M1-M5 gates; M2 pass 52-65 min and 6,300-7,600 m, M2 step 4 pass 33-41 min at the jog, M3 pass <=8% of samples under 1.6 m/s and mean 2.0 +- 0.05, M4 pass every leg within +-20% of the tabled walk minutes
reference_items.native_verdict: Every M2/M3/M4 bar passes on a body I walked myself, including M2 step 4 (the jog) which nobody in this project had ever run. The item is scored 8 rather than 10 because the same route walked in the OTHER direction does not complete.
reference_items.justification: THE CROSSING, walked end to end by the critic at HEAD: 6,646.7 m, 199,433 frames, 55.398 in-world minutes, mean 1.9991 m/s, 0.063% of 33,238 samples under 1.6 m/s, worst deviation from the road 1.39 m of a 6 m carriageway, zero frames off the road, zero teleports, ending at (2765.6, 5028.8). Reproduced with a SECOND per-frame counter installed on Engine._afterStep, whose unbounded naive sum is also 6,646.7 m and whose largest single-frame step in 199,432 frames is 0.295 m — so the zero is zero because nothing jumped, not because jumps stopped being counted. M2 52-65 -> 55.398. M2 6,300-7,600 -> 6,646.7. M2 step 4 33-41 -> 34.622 at the jog (6,645.9 m, 124,639 frames, mean 3.2000 m/s). M3 <=8% -> 0.063%; mean 2.0+-0.05 -> 1.9991. M4 +-20% -> -3.0%, -5.6%, -1.7% per leg. The hour comes from distance.
reference_items.why_not_ten: The route is walkable in one direction only. Reversed (Lilmoth -> Stormhold) the body walks 5,072.3 m of 6,903.6 m and then stops dead — 900 consecutive frames under 1 cm — at (2278.6, 1859.2), 0.62 m from the centreline, where a declared 17 m / 8 m viaduct on stormhold-helstrom points 129-131 lays its 3.5 m deck slab across the LOWER limb of the same switchback (points 126 and 131 are 5.74 m apart horizontally and 7.51 m vertically). heightAt then steps the carriageway up 5.75 m and back down 7.5 m over ten metres, inside a declared span GAP. A scale item whose headline is "about an hour on foot" cannot score above 8 while the hour only runs one way.

checks.observed: stormhold-helstrom 23.574 vs tabled 24.3 (-3.0%); helstrom-blackrose 19.539 vs 20.7 (-5.6%); blackrose-lilmoth 12.284 vs 12.5 (-1.7%). Bar is +-20%.

checks.what: rule 8 — does the route survive being varied? backwards, at the jog, at night in a storm, encumbered
checks.observed: THREE OF FOUR SURVIVE, ONE DOES NOT. Jog arrives. Night+storm+OVERLADEN walks at 1.5724 m/s with worst deviation 1.39 m and zero frames off the road. soulrest-blackrose arrives in BOTH directions. But THE CROSSING reversed is STUCK at 5,072.3 m — see why_not_ten.

checks.what: is the distance honest — does path_m exclude metres the world MOVED the body?
checks.observed: YES for walkRoute, and I watched it bite: killed at 799 m, the province respawned the body 3,856.1 m away, path_m went 799.0 -> 814.0 with teleports 1 and teleported_m 3,856.1, while my own unbounded counter read 4,670.1 m. The respawn point is 116.7 m from the crossing destination, so an unexcluded teleport would report an arrival for a body that died on the first leg.

reference_items.native_scale: §4 verticality: what the road is asked to climb, and whether a body that leaves it can return
reference_items.native_verdict: The road itself is comfortably inside the walkable limit and always was. Its SHOULDER is not, and the piece correctly leaves that open.
reference_items.justification: Recomputed independently from roads.json and field.js: the worst longitudinal road gradient anywhere in the province is 24.27 deg on stormhold-helstrom against a 40 deg walkable limit — identical to the builder’s figure, from my own arithmetic. The published stall at (2153.7, 1197.8) is 4.97 m off the centreline and 15.61 m BELOW the deck, inside the declared 471 m / 50.6 m viaduct, with onDeckAt and onRoadAt both false: it fell off a bridge. The disowned 57.5/61.09/64.6 deg readings reproduce as field.slopeAt() artefacts — 61.10 deg at r=5 and 73.55 deg at r=2.5 at the stall, against 1.09 deg on a leg with no structures at all. THERE IS NO SKIRT and the premise correction is right.
reference_items.why_not_ten: Two things. (a) One of the three supports the correction rests on cannot fail: "the slope gate refuses zero samples of any centreline" is structurally zero, because traversal.js exempts a body when onRoadAt() is true and 25,390 of 25,390 centreline samples are exempt (100.0000%). Rule 4, and it has propagated into the §P.4 gate paragraph. (b) The shoulder is genuinely un-regainable in places: G3-REGAIN 63 and G4-NO-FALL 488 both reproduce EXACTLY, and my replacement lateral sweep — restricted to the four legs with zero deck_spans so no slab edge can inflate it — refuses 0 of 14,253 samples at 3.5 m off the centreline and 4 of 14,473 at 4 m, rising to 41 of 19,712 at 5 m.

checks.what: is there a 57.5 deg skirt on the Valus Ridge?
checks.observed: NO. Worst longitudinal road gradient in the province 24.27 deg (limit 40). The stall is 4.97 m off the centreline and 15.61 m below the deck of a declared 471 m viaduct standing 50.6 m up. slopeAt reproduces 61.10 deg there and 1.09 deg on a structure-free leg. Two agents and one orchestrator brief asserted the skirt; all three were wrong.

checks.what: can the "zero slope-gate refusals on the centreline" counter ever be non-zero?
checks.observed: NO. 25,390 of 25,390 centreline samples across all ten legs are exempt from the slope gate via onRoadAt(), which returns true within half_width x 1.15 of the centreline. The counter is a restatement of the exemption, not a measurement of the province. Replacement supplied and it bites.

63 and 488, EXACTLY reproducing the builder, including 59 of the 63 on stormhold-helstrom. Correctly reported as open. Confirmed from a walked body: 2 of 20 independent 25 m shoves on LEVEL ground do not come back.

checks.what: the --stair-grade sweep, reproduced by re-running the generator rather than reading the sweep file
checks.observed: 0.45 -> 0.60 takes the network from 1,732 m of deck span to 1,431 m and the tallest structure from 50.6 m to 32.7 m, with the trunk network (25,385.3 m) and THE CROSSING (6,903.6 m) UNCHANGED — zero length cost — and the worst road gradient 24.27 -> 31.13 deg. REFERRED as a design question, not decided here.

reference_items.native_scale: binary per model: name the world-side consumer and demonstrate it by perturbing the model and watching an entity change behaviour
reference_items.native_verdict: Both shipped models are genuinely consumed, and a third (burden) falls out of my own perturbation. The shipped C2-NULL bar is broken and its author says so.
reference_items.justification: The road centreline is read by engine._pursue() and the structures by field.clampToDeck()/onDeckAt()/heightAt(); both are demonstrated by perturbation. My own third perturbation: setBurden(0.9) puts the body in OVERLADEN with move_mult_applied 0.72 and the walked mean speed drops 1.9991 -> 1.5724 m/s over 160,001 stepping frames, so the burden model is read too.
reference_items.why_not_ten: C2-NULL-IS-SILENT as shipped prints PASS against a bar of 6,193 m, because max(0.5, noise_floor x 1.5) read its floor from an arm the builder had already invalidated. It flagged this red in its own survey rather than presenting it as a result, which is the right behaviour and the reason this is a 7 and not lower. My replacement measures the floor instead of inheriting it — and its own first cut failed (the road bump sat 1,450 m into a 466 m walk, so the POSITIVE arm read 0.000 m), which is recorded rather than quietly fixed.

checks.what: is the road centreline read by the body?
checks.observed: Yes — engine._pursue() computes the body’s projection onto roads.json legs[].points every frame and steers from it; deleting or moving those points moves the body. Demonstrated by the builder (15.65 m for a 25 m bump) and by the delete-the-fix grid, where replacing _pursue collapses the walk from 1,779.2 m to 550.1 m.

NO, and the builder says so. Bar 6,193 m from an invalidated noise-floor arm. Replaced with a measured floor: the same walk run twice with nothing changed, compared track-against-track at the same frame.

checks.what: CRITIC’S OWN PERTURBATION — is the burden model read by a walking body?
checks.observed: YES. setBurden(0.9) -> tier OVERLADEN, move_mult_applied 0.72, burden_source "pinned by setBurden()"; the walked mean speed over 160,001 stepping frames is 1.5724 m/s against 1.9991 unencumbered, and the body still holds the road to 1.39 m with zero frames off it. NOTE FOR WHOEVER OWNS IT: NEXT-DISPATCH §Q1 says setBurden "has been inert on any stepping run". On this stepping run it is not. Recorded, not adjudicated — it is not my piece.

reference_items.axis_note: SCORING.md §1.1 min-over-axes note: Z2 is a FAIL on the shipped C2-NULL-IS-SILENT *bar*, not on a consumption AXIS. The axes RI-MTH07 scores are the MODELS — road centreline (Z1 pass), structures (CONSUME-STRUCTURE pass) and burden (Z3 pass) — each of which is demonstrated by perturbation with a consumer named in shipped code. Z2 is a defect in one CHECK that was supposed to guard the road axis, and the road axis is carried instead by the 550.1 m / 1,779.2 m separation in the re-seeded delete-the-fix grid and by my replacement measured noise floor. So no axis is unmeasurable, and the min over the three model axes is 7 — held down by the fact that a green check with a 6,193 m bar shipped at all.

So the correct bar for a null on this fixture is 0.000 m, not max(0.5, floor x 1.5) and certainly not the shipped 6,193 m — and the null clears the strictest possible bar exactly.

score.band_label: Below bar on two short, specific, closable items — and the headline is verified
score.aggregation_note: min over nine axes. The two 6s are the FAIL. (a) Finding F7 and survey §2c state that walkRoute AND walkPath exclude teleports from path_m; walkPath does not — it still accumulates the per-frame step with no upper bound and returns no teleports field, and it is the verb tools/world/w1-01-r4-soulrest-leg.mjs uses, the tool W1-05 is being sent to re-run. (b) The route was tested forwards only, at noon, once; reversed it jams at 5,072.3 m. Everything else in this piece is strong: the headline reproduces to the decimal under an independent counter, the teardown reproduces the published coordinate running FIRST from a clean world, the premise correction is right, four instrument flaws were self-reported and two checks refused rather than published, and the four-session drowning blocker on soulrest-blackrose is closed in both directions.

status_reasons: walkPath() still counts teleports as walked distance while finding F7 and survey §2c both state it does not — a false statement about shipped code, in the piece's own headline finding, in the verb that carries the drowning and reachability evidence.

The crossing does not walk backwards: STUCK after 900 consecutive sub-centimetre frames at 5,072.3 m of 6,903.6 m, 0.62 m from the centreline, where a 17 m viaduct deck is laid 5.74 m across and 7.51 m above the lower limb of its own switchback. Rule 8 — the fixture was a single forward walk.

One of the three supports the premise correction rests on — 'the slope gate refuses zero samples of any centreline' — is structurally zero: 25,390 of 25,390 centreline samples are exempt from the gate via onRoadAt(). Rule 4. It has propagated into the §P.4 gate paragraph.

crossing-deletefix.mjs's HP pin writes only sim.player.hp, so both its NEW arms carry a death and a ~3.4 km respawn; three of its four cells do not reproduce when the world is re-seeded between arms, including the 6 m gap it uses to argue the parapet is not load-bearing.

P4_recommendation.on_what_evidence: An independent critic walked Stormhold to Lilmoth end to end at HEAD: 6,646.7 m, 199,433 frames, 55.398 in-world minutes, settlement collision ON, mean 1.9991 m/s, 0.063% of 33,238 samples under 1.6 m/s, worst deviation 1.39 m of a 6 m carriageway, zero frames off the road, zero teleports — with the zero cross-checked against an unbounded counter and against a deliberately forced respawn that the exclusion caught. RI-WLD01 M2 (both bars and the never-before-run jog), M3 and M4 all pass.
amendments_the_paragraph_needs: State hp_pinned: true. The body that walked it was immortal. That is a legitimate measurement condition (RI-WLD01 M2 step 1 says 'combat disabled', and the builder declares it in the artifact and its survey) but §P.4 does not say so, and unpinned the body dies at 1,276.8 m to regional hazards.
State that it is forwards-only. Backwards the same route jams at 5,072.3 m.

Add that the province's respawn lands 116.7 m from the crossing's destination, so any measurement of this route that does not exclude teleports will report an arrival for a body that died on the first leg.

Drop 'the slope gate refuses zero samples of any centreline' — it is a tautology, not evidence. Replace it with the lateral sweep: on structure-free legs the gate refuses 0 of 14,253 samples at 3.5 m off the centreline and 4 of 14,473 at 4 m.
P4_recommendation.do_not_gate_the_README_on: the reverse jam — but dispatch it, because it is 1.6 km into the first leg of the canonical route and a player walking home from Lilmoth will meet it.

biggest_gap.what: engine.walkPath() still adds a teleport to path_m — it accumulates the per-frame planar step with no upper bound and returns no teleports / teleported_m field — while the round’s own headline finding F7 and survey §2c both state that "walkRoute AND walkPath now record those separately and EXCLUDE them from path_m".
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: This is the exact defect the round is famous for, left live in the other half of the pair, and it is a false statement about shipped code in the piece’s own findings. walkPath is the verb tools/world/w1-01-r4-soulrest-leg.mjs drives — the tool this verdict’s own §D tells W1-05 to re-run to close a four-session blocker — and it is what scale-audit-style reachability walks use. The round’s most-quoted sentence, "every path_m this project published before may contain them", now reads as fully retired when it is only half retired. The stakes are concrete: my kill probe shows the province respawns a dead body 116.7 m from the crossing’s destination, so an unexcluded teleport turns a death on the first leg into a reported arrival, and turns 814 m of walking into 4,670 m.

remedy.action: Port the six lines already written in walkRoute into walkPath: hold out any per-frame step over 1 m from `dist`, record it in a jumps array with its endpoints and HP, and return teleports / teleported_m / teleport_log. Then correct finding F7 and reports/w1-crossing-survey.md §2c to say what the code does.
remedy.acceptance: A walk driven through walkPath that is killed mid-route reports teleports >= 1 and a path_m that rises by less than 20 m across the respawn, while an unbounded control counter over the same frames rises by the full respawn distance (3,000 m+). Re-run tools/world/w1-01-r4-soulrest-leg.mjs afterwards and confirm every published path_m for that leg carries teleports: 0.

round_2_scope: Port the teleport exclusion from walkRoute into walkPath (six lines already written) and correct F7 / survey §2c.

Adjudicate the reverse jam: stormhold-helstrom points 126/131, a 17 m viaduct deck laid across the lower limb of its own switchback, producing a 5.75 m step up and a 7.5 m step down on the carriageway at 1,635 m.
Replace the vacuous centreline slope-gate counter with the lateral sweep, and correct the §P.4 paragraph that cites it.
Strengthen crossing-deletefix.mjs's HP pin to the one crossing-body.mjs uses and re-run the grid re-seeded; do not quote its per-arm numbers until then.
